To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and demonstrated a system that can autonomously manipulate a humanoid robot to accomplish disaster-response tasks in a simulated environment.
we have successfully integrated recent advances in autonomous planning and control with the perspective and experience of human operators.

(1) the use of a human operator can improve the performance of autonomous systems in a variety of challenging tasks and (2) the use of virtual fixtures as the common language for human-robot interaction can enable seamless integration of human and machine intelligence in a wide variety of tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how an operator can use a virtual fixture to guide the robot to a goal configuration.
the development of a human–robot interface and planning system for autonomous manipulation that is capable of executing complex tasks in a dynamic environment.
the problem of enabling human operators to guide the robot to perform manipulation tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system successfully completed 5 of 8 tasks, with 3 failures due to software bugs, one due to a hardware failure, and one due to a planning failure.
the CMU team’s entry to the DARPA Robotics challenge trials was successful and the system was able to complete all the tasks within the allotted time frame.
our system is the only team to have successfully integrated human and robot control in a way that allows for the robot to be controlled in a natural, intuitive, and efficient manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to successfully complete 5 of the 8 tasks, with the remaining tasks being completed by the operator.
the human operator is able to plan, control and monitor the robot in real time with a high-level of efficiency.
we successfully combined a human operator and a robotic platform to solve complex tasks in a disaster-response scenario.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human operator is an integral part of the planning process, and the planning process is a key component in the overall control system.

the combination of a virtual fixture-based human-robot interface and a guided manipulation motion planner can provide a highly intuitive and effective interface for human operators to guide a robot to perform complex manipulation tasks.
the human operator can leverage recent advances in autonomous robotics to solve challenging tasks.
